result.rationale: MultiEmail.tsx renders `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>` and the remove button does `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`, so removing a middle row shifts values while keys stay positional, causing React to reuse the wrong component instances for subsequent rows (misplaced focus/caret, transient stale inputs). The mechanism is verifiable directly in the diff.

judged_text: List items are keyed by array index while rows can be removed via splice, so React reuses DOM/state for the wrong email fields after a middle-row deletion. After removing an email from the middle of the list, the controlled values shift but React keys stay positional, producing misplaced focus/caret and transiently stale rendered values for the rows after the removed one — a classic index-key defect that bites the next edit of this component.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the email rows are rendered with `value.map((field, index) => (<li key={index}> ... ))`, and rows can be removed from the middle via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. This is the classic “index as key + deletions/reordering” problem: after deleting a middle row, React will reuse DOM/state for subsequent rows because their keys (indexes) shift, which can cause focus/caret jumps and transiently mismatched rendered values even though the controlled `value` array updates.
